title: n8n License: Fair-Code, Community, Enterprise (2026)
summary: The n8n license permits internal use but bans reselling and hosting for customers. Enterprise features require a paid key.
body_markdown:
## Running the same job in Activepieces under an MIT core


### Evaluating embedding reselling or hosting options


If your answer was embedding, reselling or hosting for clients, Activepieces ships its core under the MIT license, so it lets you run, fork, resell or embed that core.


Its 743 integrations sit in the same open source monorepo, and MoneyGram, Moneypenny, Alan and FundingSocieties run it in production, on a core that is MIT-licensed rather than source-available like n8n's, which means you can freely fork and modify it without vendor restrictions.


Its core is released under the MIT license, which is an open source license and permits commercial use, modification and redistribution.


Set it against n8n and the contrast is the restriction on offering the software to others, the very clause that sent you here.


Check the repository's license file for any parts that sit outside the MIT core before you build on it, since "MIT core" is a statement about the core and not about every directory.


### Ways to try n8n for free


Three things are on the table. There's a free cloud plan that asks for no card, so you can classify your use by building a real flow before you commit to anything.


Self-hosting is available if the data has to stay on your infrastructure, and you can compare the[n8n free plan](https://www.activepieces.com/blog/n8n-free-plan-in-2026-community-edition-vs-cloud) options first.


And the apps most automations start with have their own pages:[Gmail](https://www.activepieces.com/pieces) ,[Slack](https://www.activepieces.com/pieces) and[Google Sheets](https://www.activepieces.com/pieces) are all listed under activepieces.com/integrations, which shows what each one can do before you open the builder.


### What the builder shows


Below, the builder screen shows the scale of the job. A Schedule trigger labeled "Every Hour" is selected, and a "Run on weekends" toggle sits in its settings.


The integration selector is open on spreadsheet apps, with Google Sheets listing actions such as Insert Row, Update Row and Find Rows.


The "Generate Sample Data" panel shows a successful test result, so you see the trigger fire before you wire anything to it.


### The cost of switching


Be plain about the cost of switching: your n8n workflows must be rebuilt by hand. Activepieces doesn't import or convert them, so budget for reconstruction, not migration.


When you're ready to test,[create a free Activepieces account](https://cloud.activepieces.com/sign-up?ap_cta=blog_body&ref=%2Fblog%2Fn8n-license-fair-code-community-enterprise-2026) and rebuild one small workflow first.
